Xanadu和Bluefors宣布合作，开发用于公用事业规模量子计算的低温基础设施
9月29日，Xanadu和Bluefors宣布达成数百万美元的合作，开发用于公用事业规模量子计算（USQC）的低温原型。两家公司旨在开发模块化低温基础设施，以支持Xanadu计划中的USQC数据中心及未来的量子数据中心。Xanadu和Bluefors计划利用原型成果开发一款可大规模制造的低温模块，用于单光子探测器和USQC数据中心环境。

2026沃尔夫物理学奖揭晓，叶军与
Bloch共获殊荣
10月1日，2026年沃尔夫奖正式公布获奖名单。其中，美国科罗拉多大学、美国国家标准与技术研究院（NIST）的叶军和德国马克斯·普朗克量子光学研究所、慕尼黑大学的Immanuel Bloch共同获得沃尔夫物理学奖，获奖理由是“在超冷原子系统控制方面取得具有变革性且可广泛应用的进展”。两人的成就共同代表了现代物理学一个重要转折，即从观测量子世界，走向控制、测量并利用量子世界。

北京大学等提出用于强子对撞机组合问题的混合量子
-
经典方法
本研究以大型强子对撞机中顶夸克对产生的全强子衰变道为例，探索量子算法解决末态粒子组合匹配问题的能力。研究
人员
比较量子近似优化算法（
QAOA）、基于反馈的量子优化算法（FALQON）和变分量子虚时演化算法（VarQITE）等方法，发现所研究的量子算法在正确匹配效率上可优于传统运动学方法，并可达到与机器学习方法相当、与量子退火方法相当或更好的表现。算法针对每个碰撞事件单独调整参数，无需经典机器学习所依赖的大规模预训练。研究展示了量子优化在高能物理事件重建中的应用潜力，但匹配精度的改善不等同于已经获得计算速度上的量子优势。研究成果于9月28日发表于《Scientific Reports》（科学报告）。
来源：
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-69946-w

成功大学利用噪声增强量子核估计非马尔可夫性
本研究受里德伯原子模拟量子计算的启发，构建模拟量子核和混合量子核，用于从稀疏时间采样数据估计开放量子系统的非马尔可夫性。数值结果显示，两类模型在该任务中可与标准基线方法竞争
。
当原子间距调节至适当范围时，操作噪声反而能够改善预测表现。分析表明，噪声使模型在紧密拟合训练数据的同时控制测试均方误差，并可获得比理想无噪声模型更高的复杂度，以及更低或相近的训练误差。这一结果揭示了特定条件下噪声对量子核学习的有益作用，也为减少非马尔可夫性估计所需的时间采样和实验资源提供了方法。研究成果于
9月28日发表于《Scientific Reports》（科学报告）。

福州大学等提出玻色量子比特的通用压缩增强读出方法
本研究提出玻色量子比特的压缩增强读出方案，首先将编码态映射至多能级原子，再结合腔内与外部压缩进行色散测量，使相邻能级间的色散耦合强度和测量信噪比实现指数增强。该方法可显著缩短单次读出时间、降低测量误差，使玻色量子比特的单次读出保真度提升一个数量级以上，为玻色编码量子计算的高保真读出提供新方案。研究成果于
9月28日发表于《Physical Review Research》（物理评论研究）。

d维量子系统，实现最坏情况下的最优阴影估计需要且仅需Θ(d²)个测量基，并给出显式构造
，

IBM苏黎世研究院等识别并缓解空穴自旋量子比特读出误差
本研究系统分析锗双量子点空穴自旋量子比特双锁存读出中的误差过程。研究通过调节磁场方向，将
|↓↓⟩态绝热映射至唯一非阻塞态，并通过低场操作抑制随磁场强度显著变化的自旋弛豫。结合双锁存误差缓解、射频电荷传感和磁场参数优化，系统在保持双自旋控制的同时，实现97.0%的单量子比特态制备与测量单次保真度，为提高锗空穴自旋量子比特读出性能提供了实验依据。研究成果于9月29日发表于《Nature Electronics》（自然·电子学）。

# Weekly Report | Wolf Physics Prize — "Nobel Predictor" Honors Jun Ye and Bloch; Photonic Quantum Computing Leader Xanadu Partners with Cryogenics Giant Bluefors…

---

## Xanadu and Bluefors Announce Partnership to Develop Cryogenic Infrastructure for Utility-Scale Quantum Computing

On September 29, Xanadu and Bluefors announced a multi-million-dollar collaboration to develop cryogenic prototypes for utility-scale quantum computing (USQC). The two companies aim to develop modular cryogenic infrastructure to support Xanadu's planned USQC data centers and future quantum data centers. Xanadu and Bluefors plan to leverage prototype outcomes to develop a mass-manufacturable cryogenic module for single-photon detectors and USQC data center environments.

**Source:**
https://investors.xanadu.ai/news-releases/news-release-details/xanadu-and-bluefors-partner-redefine-cryogenic-infrastructure

## 2026 Wolf Prize in Physics Awarded to Jun Ye and Immanuel Bloch

On October 1, the 2026 Wolf Prize laureates were officially announced. Jun Ye of the University of Colorado and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), and Immanuel Bloch of the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich jointly received the Wolf Prize in Physics "for transformative and broadly applicable advances in the control of ultracold atomic systems." Their combined achievements represent a pivotal turning point in modern physics — the transition from observing the quantum world to controlling, measuring, and exploiting it.

**Source:**
https://wolffund.org.il/home-page/

---

## India Designates Quantum Technology as One of Its Next Major Infrastructure Investment Priorities

On September 28, India's Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated, as reported by the *Hindustan Times*, that India's next wave of major infrastructure investments will include quantum technology, artificial intelligence, and semiconductor chips. Sitharaman called on academia and industry to collaborate in building capabilities, though the report cited no new quantum funding allocations or investment timelines. She rejected characterizations of India as a laggard in AI and quantum, arguing that stock market listings are an insufficient measure of domestic technological activity.

**Source:**
https://www.hindustantimes.com/education/news/ai-semiconductors-quantum-tech-next-major-frontier-for-india-sitharaman-101790572037646.html

## China's State Council Information Office Holds "15th Five-Year Plan" Press Conference; Ministry of Science and Technology Announces Focus on Quantum Science and Technology

On September 29, the State Council Information Office of China held a press conference in its series themed "Launching the 15th Five-Year Plan," presenting plans for advancing China's drive to become a science and technology powerhouse. Minister of Science and Technology Yin Hejun stated that efforts will focus on frontier domains including artificial intelligence, quantum science and technology, and biomanufacturing; key sectors including integrated circuits and industrial machine tools; and strategic domains including deep space, deep sea, and deep earth — with full-chain advancement of research into core and critical technologies.

**Source:**
http://www.scio.gov.cn/live/2026/39624/index.html

## NATO Releases Quantum Technology Roadmap, Establishing Operational Timelines and Standardization Framework

On September 29, NATO released its Quantum Technology Roadmap, built upon the quantum strategy approved by NATO in 2023 and providing a structured pathway for quantum computing, quantum communications, and quantum sensing. The roadmap also addresses how quantum technologies will interact with other dual-use technologies — such as artificial intelligence, space, and next-generation communications networks — as a core element of NATO's work. In accordance with the strategy, the roadmap is designed to support implementation by translating strategic imperatives into actionable components and helping the Alliance achieve quantum readiness.

**Sources:**
https://www.nato.int/en/news-and-events/articles/news/2026/09/29/nato-releases-quantum-technology-roadmap

## California Governor Signs Legislation to Accelerate Fusion Industry; Allocates Funding to Advance State Quantum Infrastructure

On September 30, California's Governor signed legislation and announced a joint budget allocation of $30 million for quantum and deep-space research to advance the state's technology infrastructure. The executive action was announced at a quantum laboratory at the University of California, Berkeley, and aims to expand the state's Quantum California initiative by supporting university research centers, public-private startup incubators, and hardware supply chain infrastructure spanning the physical sciences and semiconductor manufacturing.

**Source:**
https://www.gov.ca.gov/2026/09/30/governor-newsom-signs-legislation-to-accelerate-californias-fusion-industry-announces-major-investment-for-quantum-research/

## CEA-Leti and Quobly Strengthen Collaboration to Accelerate Next-Generation Silicon Quantum Technology

On September 28, Quobly announced it is expanding its collaboration with CEA-Leti (Commissariat à l'énergie atomique et aux énergies alternatives – Laboratory for Electronics and Information Technology) by gaining access to the FAMES pilot line to develop technologies for future silicon quantum processors. FAMES provides semiconductor equipment for testing manufacturing processes, complementing Quobly's work with STMicroelectronics to industrialize its silicon spin qubit architecture. Quobly plans to commercialize its first quantum computer, the Alloy Pioneer, by the end of 2026, with a target of one million qubits by 2032.

**Source:**
https://www.quobly.io/press-releases/cea-leti-and-quobly-strengthen-their-collaboration-to-accelerate-the-development-of-next-generation-silicon-quantum-technologies/

## Pasqal Evolves Collaboration Framework with French Public Authorities Toward Commercial Quantum Computing

On September 28, Pasqal announced it is transitioning its collaboration with French public institutions toward commercial applications, moving away from participation in the LSQUARE/PROQCIMA defense program. The company has completed the technical objectives of PROQCIMA Phase 1 and has been invited to participate in a civilian public support program currently being defined. French authorities have asked Pasqal to submit a fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) R&D plan based on neutral atoms to support its commercial technology roadmap.

On September 28, according to the *Seoul Economic Daily*, Quandela plans to develop strategic partnerships in South Korea over the next two years spanning quantum manufacturing, system integration, and operations. The company seeks to collaborate with Korean partners in photonic component manufacturing, advanced packaging, wafer-level inspection, optical alignment, and integrated quantum control systems. Quandela is also considering forming a Korean Quantum Manufacturing Alliance, as well as potential collaboration with quantum clusters in Seoul, Gwangju (South Jeolla Province), and the southeastern region.

On September 29, Project Eleven announced the acquisition of Riva Labs to extend its capabilities in post-quantum cryptography, wallets, multi-party computation (MPC), account abstraction, and blockchain infrastructure. Riva Labs brings technology and intellectual property in Ethereum and other public blockchain domains, including post-quantum signatures and hardware signing. The Riva team will join Project Eleven's research and product efforts focused on post-quantum cryptography, digital asset custody, and blockchain security.

On September 29, Infleqtion announced the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Riverlane to explore integrating Riverlane's real-time quantum error correction technology with Infleqtion's neutral-atom quantum computing platform and software stack. The two companies will evaluate Riverlane's Deltaflow and Deltakit tools alongside Infleqtion's Superstaq compiler and open-source qLDPC software library. The collaboration plan includes technical workshops and potential demonstrations focused on utility-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computing within UK quantum computing programs.

On September 29, Terra Quantum and Empa (Swiss Federal Laboratories for Materials Science and Technology) collaborated to develop LP-FNO, a Fourier Neural Operator model capable of predicting three-dimensional temperature fields and melt pool boundaries from laser welding parameters. The model was trained on high-fidelity simulations of Ti-6Al-4V with laser power ranging from 40–190 W and scanning speeds of 0.1–1 m/s. Once trained, LP-FNO generates complete three-dimensional predictions in approximately 8 ms at standard resolution and 88 ms at double resolution.

On September 29, Cloudflare announced plans to establish a public Certificate Authority (CA) to issue both traditional TLS certificates and post-quantum Merkle Tree Certificates (MTC). The company plans to obtain publicly trusted Root CA key material from GlobalSign and has applied for inclusion in the root programs of Chrome, Apple, Microsoft, and Mozilla. On September 29, DecaQ announced the release of Cloud Beta 2, supporting 400 logical digital qubits, six quantum algorithm families, and up to 200,000 digital oracle gates on general-purpose hardware. The platform uses Digital Quantum Oracles to execute supported workloads without requiring physical qubits or quantum processors, providing oracle evaluation, phase estimation, energy estimation, and optimization capabilities. Researchers, developers, and enterprise R&D teams can apply for test access; reference workloads cover local field energy, encoded latency readout, and wireless channel partitioning.

At the event, the province's first quantum ecosystem platform — the "Huguang Yunchuang" Quantum Ecosystem Platform — was officially unveiled. Initiated by Xihu Yunchuang Group and implemented under the guidance of the Zhejiang Provincial Information Security Industry Association with the participation of universities, research institutions, and industry chain enterprises from across and beyond the province, the platform comprises three sub-platforms: quantum computing power, quantum security, and quantum project incubation.

On September 30, Hefei Yaozheng Quantum Technology Co., Ltd. (合肥幺正量子科技有限公司) announced that its independently developed ion trap quantum computer has passed the Quantum Volume (QV) 128 benchmark, setting a new record among publicly reported domestic achievements and marking a new milestone in the overall system performance with continued acceleration of technology iteration. On September 30, Classiq introduced its Fault Tolerance Engine, a compiler and translation suite integrated directly into the Classiq SDK. The tool maps high-level, optimized logical quantum circuits — written in Classiq's Qmod language or as Clifford+T QASM — to concrete three-dimensional spacetime execution plans across fault-tolerant quantum processing units (QPUs). By moving beyond static algorithmic resource formulas, the engine generates hardware-aware routing schedules, magic state distillation plans, and empirical physical qubit and error rate estimates.

Experiments show that the signal amplitude of this scheme does not attenuate with increasing symbol rate as in conventional heterodyne Rydberg receivers, but is more sensitive to low-frequency pink noise. This study establishes a theory of quantum-enhanced interferometry applicable to general Markovian quantum light sources, for determining under what conditions realistic sources can achieve measurement advantages beyond the classical limit. ## University of Bristol (UK) Derives Upper Bounds on Recurrence Times of Finite Quantum Systems
